summary: RETEST of bug from iteration_2.json. FIX DID NOT WORK. The 2nd mount of <Player> after editing station A still throws an uncaught 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' pageerror and the webpack-dev-server red 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay still covers the player UI. The ErrorBoundary fallback (player-error-fallback) is NEVER triggered because the error is an asynchronous cross-origin 'Script error.' caught by window.onerror — NOT a synchronous React render error — so React componentDidCatch does not fire. Bug persists exactly as reported in iteration_2.json. POST /api/spotify/tracks still returns 200 with 48 tracks on the 2nd mount (confirmed in console). Spotify SDK polling permanently returns 'No state available' after the crash, i.e. SDK is in dead state on remount.

ui_bugs.issue: 2nd mount of <Player> in the same session still throws uncaught pageerror 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)'. Webpack dev-server overlay iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay is rendered on top of the page, intercepting ALL pointer events — Back to Stations button becomes unclickable. Polling logs 'Polling: No state available' continuously after the error, confirming Spotify Web Playback SDK is in dead/broken state on remount.

ErrorBoundary does NOT catch the error because it is thrown asynchronously from inside the Spotify SDK / react-spotify-web-playback (cross-origin 'Script error.' via window.onerror), not during React's render/commit phase. data-testid 'player-error-fallback' never appears even when the crash happens. ErrorBoundary is functional but architecturally cannot catch this class of error.

The new spotifyPlayerRef.current?.disconnect?.() on unmount executes, but it is NOT sufficient to prevent the crash. Either react-spotify-web-playback's internal listeners outlive disconnect(), OR the SDK's global window.Spotify singleton retains stale state. The WeakSet guard in connectAudioToVisualizer is fine but irrelevant — the error originates BEFORE/independently of createMediaElementSource (no related console warning fires; the error is logged immediately after '✅ Starting album art polling').

integration_issues.flow: Edit station -> reopen same station (2nd mount of Player)
integration_issues.issue: Reproduces 100% reliably. Pageerror exact text: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')". Stack (cross-origin masked): 'Script error. at handleError (bundle.js:38038:58) at bundle.js:38057:7'. Two '✓ Spotify player instance captured' logs in the 2nd mount confirm the SpotifyPlayer is fully re-initialized — the disconnect() did not prevent SDK breakage.

action_items: Bug NOT fixed. The current mitigations (WeakSet for createMediaElementSource, ErrorBoundary, spotifyPlayer.disconnect on unmount) are insufficient because the error originates inside react-spotify-web-playback / Spotify Web Playback SDK itself on remount, asynchronously, and ErrorBoundary cannot catch async errors.

RECOMMENDED FIX (the one suggested as 'Option A' in iteration_2.json): keep <Player> mounted permanently. In App.js, do NOT unmount Player when navigating to 'stations'/'edit'/'create' — instead render it always but toggle CSS display:none / visibility:hidden when currentView !== 'player'. This avoids the entire SpotifyPlayer remount problem.

ALTERNATIVE FIX: replace react-spotify-web-playback (unmaintained, last 2022) with a direct integration of the official Spotify Web Playback SDK and explicitly call player.disconnect() AND remove all event listeners on unmount; ensure window.Spotify.Player singleton is also torn down.

DEFENSIVE: install a global window.onerror handler in App.js that swallows 'Script error.' from sdk.scdn.co AND, more importantly, suppresses the webpack-dev-server error overlay (window.__REACT_ERROR_OVERLAY__ or react-error-overlay's stopReportingRuntimeErrors). That at least keeps the UI usable in dev mode, though it does not fix the underlying SDK state corruption.

ErrorBoundary as currently written WILL NOT help — it only catches React render-phase errors. To catch the async SDK error, you'd need to listen to window 'error' / 'unhandledrejection' inside Player and setState to surface a fallback.
critical_code_review_comments: Player.jsx unmount disconnect runs via a useEffect with empty deps + cleanup — this fires on Player unmount as expected, but disconnect() alone is insufficient for react-spotify-web-playback to fully tear down.

Player.jsx 'getPlayer' guards capture with `!spotifyPlayer` but spotifyPlayer is component state reset on remount, so the guard is effectively useless on remount (state is freshly null). On remount you ALWAYS hit setSpotifyPlayer(player) + setPlayerReady(true), which is fine but means a new SDK instance is created every mount.
Player.jsx ~700 lines — should be split into PlayerCore / Visualizer / BumperManager modules.

App.js still unmounts Player on every view switch. Even if SDK cleanup were perfect, repeated unmount/mount of a non-React iframe-backed SDK is fragile. Keeping Player mounted (option A) is the most robust architectural fix.
test_credentials: Auto-auth via ?spotify_auth=success — stored Spotify token auto-refreshes. No app login.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Confirm the bug-not-fixed result by: open station A -> Back -> Edit station A -> click create-station-btn (Update Station) -> click station A again. The 2nd mount triggers pageerror "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')" and the iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay covers the page (blocks back-from-player-btn clicks). ErrorBoundary fallback player-error-fallback never appears. Recommend Main Agent implement the 'keep-Player-mounted, toggle display' refactor in App.js as it is the only fix that sidesteps the SDK-remount crash entirely.

rca_of_the_issue.bug: Editing then reopening a station still crashes the player; SAME bug as iteration_2.json — current fix is ineffective.
observed_evidence: 1st mount of Player: webpack-overlay=False, no pageerrors, player-container renders, album art appears.

After edit + 2nd mount: webpack-overlay=True (iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay present), pageerror 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)', player-container DOES render behind overlay, but 'Polling: No state available' loops forever -> SDK dead.
Console shows '✓ Spotify player instance captured' twice in 2nd mount -> SpotifyPlayer fully re-initialized; spotifyPlayerRef.current?.disconnect?.() on unmount did fire but did not prevent crash.
ErrorBoundary fallback (player-error-fallback) was NOT present -> ErrorBoundary cannot catch async cross-origin 'Script error.'
Test ran into timeout clicking back-from-player-btn because overlay intercepts pointer events — proving the overlay is the user-visible 'broken player'.
rca_of_the_issue.real_fix_needed: Stop unmounting <Player> on view switches (keep mounted, toggle display via CSS). This bypasses the SDK re-init that triggers the crash.
